author: GamingBolt
description:
Riot Games has been looking for ways to expand the dominance of its League of Legends IP. By tapping into a competitive genre once more, 2XKO is its latest attempt at doing so. The fighting game offers a low barrier to entry thanks to it being free-to-play, along with hiding quite a bit of its depth behind more complex mechanics that only become available once you actually do the tutorials. 

The starting roster is a strong one, but it also gives a worrisome look at future monetisation. Some characters are locked, and while you can unlock them simply by playing the game, the fact that you can also pay real-world money has some negative implications, and could even potentially encourage the developers to make sure its new roster additions are overpowered to create an incentive to unlock them with real money. 

Aside from that, 2XKO is off to a phenomenal start, and will be kept alive by its strong multiplayer infrastructure and rollback netcode.
title: 2XKO Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
The goblin thievery of Styx surprisingly lives on with a new sequel in Styx: Blades of Greed. If you’re a fan of stealth games like Dishonored, don’t sleep on this one. You have abilities like clone distractions, invisibility, and enemy possession along with a flexible skill tree along with other gadgets to distract enemies with. 

Perhaps the biggest evolution from the previous game is the expanded scope and vertical environments. Styx: Blades of Greed is from a smaller studio and so the price reflects that at just $39.99 for PC and $49.99 on consoles. Check out the demo if you’re curious and want to see what the foul-mouthed goblin is up to this time.
title: Styx: Blades of Greed - 15 Things You Need To Know BEFORE YOU BUY

author: GamingBolt
description:
Resident Evil Requiem might have been a very different game from the one we're about to dive into, if reports about the developer pondering an open-world experience at the early stages of its development are to be believed. 

But that wasn't to be and we're glad it didn't take shape. There are a lot of reasons why Requiem wouldn't work as an open-world title, and so many more that support the decision to return to the franchise's signature style of presentation. 

While the future might hold a Resident Evil experience that's designed around an open world, it seems that Requiem is sticking to a more traditional celebration of everything that has been good about it. Join us as we take a look at why that's a very good thing.
title: Resident Evil Requiem Isn't An Open World Game, And That’s Why It’ll Be Scarier
